title: How Do Online Reviews Help Local SEO & AI Search?
summary: Reviews help local SEO more than most owners realize. Learn how review count, ratings, and recency drive trust and AI recommendations for more customers.
body_markdown:
Key Takeaways


##


1. Review count and ratings can improve local search rankings, helping more nearby customers find your business.
2. A strong review profile combines steady review volume, good ratings, recent feedback, and useful customer details.
3. Consistently asking for and responding to reviews can build customer trust and help turn more local searches into customers.
4. Reviews also shape AI-powered recommendations. 45% of customers use generative AI to find local businesses.

## How Do Online Reviews Help Local SEO & AI Recommendations for Small Businesses?


Customers decide whether to trust your business before they ever speak to you. How? They search online, read a few reviews, and compare you against your competitors. Then they pick a business they trust – which might not be yours.


At that point, they don’t consider your pricing or the years of experience you have – in fact, they don’t even know any of that. Instead, what they look for is the star rating and what your last customers said about you. When they see that your competitor has more reviews and recent customer comments, you may have already lost that customer before they even spoke with you.


So, do reviews help SEO? Yes, especially[local SEO](https://www.thryv.com/blog/local-seo-know-youre-winning/) (search engine optimization). The same reviews that convince a customer to contact your competitor also affect whether you show up in Google’s search engine results pages ([SERPs](https://www.thryv.com/blog/serp/) ) and in[AI-powered search](https://www.thryv.com/blog/what-is-ai-search/) .


How do you gain visibility in local Google and AI searches so that you don’t lose out against your competitors? Understanding which review activities improve your online visibility and which help turn searchers into customers can help you spend your time on what brings in more calls, customers, and revenue.


## Do Reviews Affect SEO Or Just Audience Trust?


Your business can show up in Google Search and still lose the call. A dental practice with a 4.2-star rating and reviews from six months ago may appear beside one with a stronger rating and recent feedback about same-day emergency appointments. Those[reviews can influence](https://www.thryv.com/blog/why-online-reviews-matter-local-seo/) which business the customer chooses.


Reviews have the clearest direct impact on local search results and Google Maps.[Google confirms](https://support.google.com/business/answer/7091?hl=en) that review count and ratings can contribute to your local rankings, but reviews shouldn’t be treated as a ranking factor for every page on your website. These review signals also provide social proof once customers find you, building customer trust and helping them decide whether to call, book, or keep searching. That can affect click-through rates, or how often someone chooses your business from the search results.


According to[Bright Local’s 2026 Local Consumer Review Survey](https://www.brightlocal.com/research/local-consumer-review-survey/) , 97% of consumers read reviews before choosing a local business. That makes your review profile important at two points in the customer journey: getting found and getting chosen.

## How Many Reviews Do You Need to Compete Locally?


No specific review volume guarantees higher search rankings. However, BrightLocal’s survey discovered that 47% of consumers won’t use a business with fewer than 20 reviews. Reaching that many reviews can be a challenge for small business owners. A more useful goal is to see how your review profile compares with businesses already appearing for searches that bring you the most valuable customers.


If you’re a plumber, search Google for terms such as “emergency plumber near me” or “water heater repair.” The same approach applies to a salon, law firm, or any other small business. Then:


1. Look at the businesses appearing prominently in the local search results.
2. Compare their review totals and ratings with yours.
3. Check how recently they’re receiving customer feedback.
4. Use the gap to set a realistic review goal.


If you have 32 reviews and businesses appearing in the[Google local pack](https://www.thryv.com/blog/optimize-small-business-local-search/) , or Map Pack, have 150 to 250, reaching 40 reviews is progress, but there’s still room to strengthen your position. Repeat this check every few months as your business and competitors add reviews.


## Which Review Factors Matter Most For Local Businesses’ SEO?


[Google confirms](https://support.google.com/business/answer/7091?hl=en) that review count and ratings can contribute to local rankings. Local search practitioners also point to four important signals: review content, recency, steady review growth, and how you respond.


### Review Quantity


More genuine reviews give Google and potential customers more information about your small business. Reviews are also a form of[user-generated content](https://www.thryv.com/blog/user-generated-content-local-business-marketing/) , giving prospective customers firsthand insight into their experiences with your business. Build review requests into your customer follow-up, so your review volume and customer feedback keep growing throughout the year.


If you finish 20 jobs this week but ask only two customers for reviews, you’re leaving 18 opportunities for valuable feedback on the table.


###
Review Content


Detailed reviews can provide useful context about your work. A customer who mentions a last-minute hair color correction gives prospective customers specific information about your services. That kind of detail may also naturally include[long-tail keywords](https://www.thryv.com/blog/long-tail-keywords-how-people-are-finding-your-website/) people use when searching for a specific service or problem.


Let those details come from the customer. Ask people to describe their experience in their own words rather than suggesting keywords or phrases to include.


### Review Rating and Quality


Google says higher ratings can support local search rankings, and customers see those ratings when deciding who to contact.


Pay attention to patterns in the feedback you receive. Several complaints about unanswered calls, late arrivals, or poor follow-up may point to a customer experience issue that could cost you future business. If you don’t address them, those patterns drag down your average star ratings.


### Review Recency


Recent reviews show ongoing customer activity, and customers actively look for them. BrightLocal’s 2026 survey found that 74% of customers only care about reviews written in the last three months. Build requests into your regular process so you collect feedback steadily instead of relying on occasional review campaigns.


### Review Responses


Google encourages businesses to respond to reviews, although there isn’t clear evidence that owner responses directly improve rankings. Review responses still influence how potential customers see your business and can help build customer trust.


A professional response to a complaint shows how you handle customer concerns. Thoughtful owner responses to positive feedback also show customers that you’re paying attention to their experience.


**Critical Review Factors Influencing SEO & AI Performance**


**Review Factor** **What The Business Owner Should Do**

## Do Reviews Help You Show Up In AI Recommendations?


AI engines like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude rely on public information when making local business recommendations. Reviews are part of the information they read. Use of AI for local recommendations increases every year: BrightLocal’s 2026 survey found that customers increasingly rely on local AI recommendations – from 6% to 45% within one year.


Say someone asks an AI tool to recommend an emergency plumber nearby with good reviews. Reviews and other online information can provide context about local businesses, including whether customers mention emergency service, the work they had done, and their experience with the company.


That makes reviews relevant to[AI search](https://www.thryv.com/blog/what-is-ai-search/) and AEO (answer engine optimization), which focuses on making business information clear and useful for AI-powered answers. This guide to[SEO vs. AEO vs. GEO](https://www.thryv.com/blog/seo-vs-aeo-vs-geo-why-its-all-still-seo/) explains how those approaches relate to traditional search.


Keeping your reviews, listings, and other business information current gives AI tools more accurate information about your services and reputation when customers ask for local recommendations.

## Do Reviews Outside Google Matter?


Google reviews deserve attention because they appear on your[Google Business Profile](https://www.thryv.com/blog/google-business-profile-optimization/) and can influence your visibility in local search results. Customers may also check other review platforms before deciding who to hire.


A homeowner searching for an HVAC company might find you through Google Search and then check a home-service directory. Someone choosing a med spa may see reviews on Google, social media, and health and wellness sites.


Search for your business and a few competitors to see which platforms appear most often. Focus your review strategy on the places your customers actually use.


Keeping your information current across those sites gets harder as your business grows. That means less time checking individual sites and a better chance that customers find the right information when they’re ready to call or visit.


## How Do You Turn Reviews Into An SEO Advantage?


A strong[feedback strategy](https://wpe.thryv.com/blog/customer-feedback-strategy-2/) works best when asking for a review becomes part of how you finish each job or appointment.


- **Benchmark where you stand: Use the comparison above to see where you stand.** Compare your review count, rating, and recency with businesses appearing prominently in local results.
- **Ask after each completed job or appointment:** Send the request while the customer experience is fresh. A direct[Google review link generator](https://www.thryv.com/free-tools/google-review-link-generator/) creates a Google Reviews link you can send by text or email, making it easier for customers to leave feedback.
- **Respond to reviews:** Thank customers for positive feedback, and address concerns professionally.
- **Check progress monthly:** Watch review growth and recency alongside calls, inquiries, and other leads coming from Google.


Asking for reviews should feel authentic.[Never buy reviews](https://reviewsdominator.com/post/is-it-legal-to-pay-for-reviews-ftc-rules) or trade incentives as this puts your Google Business Profile at risk. The same applies to asking only customers you know are happy.


Some small business owners feel awkward asking for customer reviews. They shouldn’t. Customers who had a good experience are glad to say so. The routine of asking for reviews gets harder to maintain when you’re serving several customers a day.


That’s the part that Thryv handles: after a completed appointment, for example, Thryv can[automatically send a review request](https://www.thryv.com/features/automated-reviews/) for you. When the review comes in,[online reputation management software](https://www.thryv.com/features/reputation-management/) drafts a personalized customer reply for you to review, edit, and post. This gives more customers a chance to leave feedback without relying on you to remember every request or response.

###

Reviews on relevant sites like Yelp, Facebook, and the Better Business Bureau also matter, and give customers more information when researching your business, so focus on the platforms your customers actually use.
